''' <summary> ''' This is a helper function that gets the time from a DateTime value and returns it as a string. ''' </summary> ''' <param name="fullDate">DateTime value used to get the time.</param> ''' <returns>String representation of the time portion of a DateTime value.</returns> ''' <remarks>This is a helper function to make the code for the public method <c>ParseTimeValue</c> ''' more modular. Note that validation occurs here instead of the calling function.</remarks> Private Shared Function GetTimeString(ByVal fullDate As DateTime) As String
Dim stringDate As String
'Return empty string for null or illegal times If Not IsDate(fullDate) Then Return "" End If
stringDate = fullDate.ToString()
Dim i As Integer i = 8
'Find what position the time starts. While (True) If stringDate.Substring(i, 1) = " " Then Exit While End If i += 1 End While
Return stringDate.Substring(i + 1, (stringDate.Length - i - 1))
End Function

Dim hours As Integer Dim minutes As Integer Dim seconds As Integer

hours = Hour(fullDate) minutes = Minute(fullDate) seconds = Second(fullDate)

''' </returns> ''' <remarks>This is a helper function to make the code for the public method <c>MakeDateTime</c> ''' more modular.</remarks> Private Shared Function GetDateMMDDYY(ByVal fullDate As Decimal) As Object
Dim divDate As Integer Dim month As Decimal Dim day As Decimal Dim year As Decimal
'Prepare date for integer division and wierd numbers like -999999 divDate = Math.Abs(fullDate)

If year < 40 Then year = 2000 + year Else year = 1900 + year End If
'Pass the month, day and year to the original 'MakeDateTime function for validation. Return MakeDateTime("YYYY", month, day, year)
End Function

''' </exception> ''' <returns>Nullable DateTime with validation rules for SQL Server DateTime type</returns> ''' <remarks>Use this function to make an SQL Server datetime from individual ''' DB2 decimal date parts. The size of the year fields in DB2 will vary, so ''' the formatYear parameter is required to distinguish long or short year.</remarks> Private Shared Function MakeDateTime(ByVal formatYear As String, ByVal month As Decimal, _ ByVal day As Decimal, ByVal year As Decimal) As Object
Dim fullYear As Decimal
'FormatYear could be input "YY" or "YYYY" If UCase(formatYear) = "YY" Then If year <= 39 Then fullYear = 2000 + year Else fullYear = 1900 + year End If ElseIf UCase(formatYear) = "YYYY" Then fullYear = year Else Throw New System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException("formatYear", formatYear, "Valid patterns are " _ + "YY or YYYY") End If
' 30 days has September, April, June and November all the rest ' have 31 except for February which is fine it has 28 days ' although leap year makes it 29. An imperfect, but "close enough“ ' way to calculate leap years is when the following is true: ' 0 == year (mod 4)
' Validate the months If (month < 1 Or month > 12) Then Return DBNull.Value End If
' No months have a day less than 1 or greater than 31 If (day < 1 Or day > 31) Then Return DBNull.Value End If
' The low datetime value in MSSQL 1/1/1753 If (fullYear < 1753) Then Return DBNull.Value End If
' Validate the days per month If ((month = 4 Or month = 6 Or month = 9 Or month = 11) And _ (day > 30)) Then Return DBNull.Value
' February is a special case ElseIf (month = 2) Then
' Leap year If (Int(fullYear) Mod 4 = 0) Then If day > 29 Then Return DBNull.Value End If
' Normal year Else If day > 28 Then Return DBNull.Value End If End If End If
' If we're here, then we have a valid date. Now convert the passed parameters to an actual date. Dim dateString As String = "" dateString = dateString + Convert.ToString(month) + "/" + Convert.ToString(day) + "/" _ + Convert.ToString(year)
Return DateTime.Parse(dateString)
End Function

The century argument will be evaluated for two different representations ''' of century. If the century is less than 19, then it will be evaluated like a century represented as ''' 0 for 1900 and 1 for 2000. Otherwise the century will be evaluated like a century represented as the ''' thousands and hundreds place of a full year. As an example of the first case, if a value of 8 was ''' passed for the year and a value of 1 for the century, the result would be a full year of 2008. ''' For the second case, passing a value of 8 for the year and a value of 20 for the century will yield ''' a full year of 2008.</remarks> Private Shared Function MakeDateTime(ByVal month As Decimal, ByVal day As Decimal, ByVal shortYear _ As Decimal, ByVal century As Decimal) As Object
Dim fullYear As Decimal
If century < 19 Then 'Convert the year to full year based on 0 or 1 for the century. fullYear = 1900 + (100 * century) + shortYear Else 'Convert the year to full year based on 19 or 20 for the century. fullYear = century * 100 + shortYear End If Return MakeDateTime("YYYY", month, day, fullYear)
End Function

Dim month, day, shortYear, fullYear As Decimal Dim divDate As Integer

Dim divDate As Integer Dim stringDate As String Dim year As Integer Dim month As Integer Dim day As Integer
stringDate = fullDate.ToString()
'Strip the date part out of the string. Dim i As Integer i = 8
While (True) If stringDate.Substring(i, 1) = " " Then Exit While End If i += 1 End While

''' </exception> ''' <returns>Empty string if the value of stringExpression is DBNull, otherwise the value of ''' stringExpression with the leading and ending spaces removed.</returns> ''' <remarks>Use this function for replicating character fields that have unreliable left and right ''' padding. In this way, stored procedures which need to join on the field can do so without ''' using the LTRIM and RTRIM database functions. This allows the query optimizer to correctly ''' access statistics for the field, which provides a more efficient query plan.</remarks> ''' <example><c>Trim([columnName])</c></example> Public Shared Function Trim(ByVal stringExpression As Object) As Object
Dim trimmedExpression As String
If Type.GetTypeCode(stringExpression.GetType) = TypeCode.DBNull Then Return "" ElseIf Type.GetTypeCode(stringExpression.GetType) = TypeCode.String Then trimmedExpression = DirectCast(stringExpression, String) trimmedExpression = trimmedExpression.Trim() Return trimmedExpression Else Throw New System.ArgumentException("Object must contain a String type.", "stringExpression") End If
End Function
